newsitem.title: USA: St. Louis, Mo., sets two revenue bond issues.
newsitem.headline: St. Louis, Mo., sets two revenue bond issues.

text.p: St. Louis, Mo., is readying two bond issues for market, the city's comptroller's office said.
Friday, the city's Board of Aldermen approved a $19 million lease-hold revenue bond issue for a restoration project at Forest Park.
The St. Louis Municipal Finance Corp deal, led by A.G. Edwards & Sons and Stifel, Nicolaus & Co, is scheduled to be priced the week of March 10, the comptroller's office said.
On Feb 26, the city is scheduled to refund $60 million of Regional Convention and Sports Facilities bonds with Smith Barney Inc as the senior manager, the comptroller's office also said.

Meanwhile, Standard & Poor's Corp last week assigned an A-minus rating with a stable outlook to the city. According to Art Dial, an anaylst at S&P, the rating is new and does not cover any outstanding debt of St. Louis. The rating agency had previously maintained a BBB-plus rating on city debt that has since matured, he added.
